transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I don’t talk much to people. I get kind of flat and quiet, and even starting my cleaning route at work feels… like pushing a loaded cart uphill.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About… a year and a half, I guess. Maybe a little less. It started after I had to move out of my old apartment and leave that neighborhood. Since then it’s just kind of built up.
Do you still enjoy activities or hobbies that you used to find pleasurable?

Not really. I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays, or just doing crosswords with my coffee… even showing the younger guys at work little tricks, like stripping a floor right. Now I mostly just… let it all sit. It doesn’t really give me much back anymore.
Do you feel any pleasure when you do things that other people would normally enjoy?

Not much, no. Things like fishing or doing a crossword with my coffee… they used to feel good. Even showing the younger guys a trick at work. Now I mostly just don’t bother. It doesn’t really give me anything back.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live or hurting yourself?
I… yeah, sometimes. I don’t have some big plan or anything, but a lot of mornings I wake up thinking maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up at all. It scares me to say that, but… yeah.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns?
Yeah… appetite’s been off. Most days food just doesn’t taste like much, like cardboard, so I’ll skip meals or just have a few crackers after work. My pants are fitting looser, I guess.
Do you feel like you're moving slower or faster than you used to?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed. Maybe I’m just tired, but I couldn’t say if I’m moving slower or faster.
Do you often feel worthless or guilty about things?

Yeah… I guess I do. I keep thinking I messed everything up—losing my old place, not keeping things together. Even little stuff, like if the pantry’s short or I miss a hallway at work, it feels like it’s somehow my fault.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't?
Yeah… sometimes. Mostly when I’m mopping after hours. I’ll hear a man’s voice say my name, or tell me I missed a spot. It sounds real, like he’s by the stairwell, but when I look… nobody’s there.
Have you had any periods in the last two weeks where you felt better for a couple of days?
Not really… not for a couple days at a time. It’s been kind of hanging over me since not long after I moved—over a year now, I guess. Maybe a year and a couple months.
Do you feel like you're resting or sitting still more often than you used to?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t know if it’s sitting still exactly, but I get worn out quicker. Even if I sleep, by the time I get to the building my arms and legs feel heavy. Little jobs, like taking out trash bags, feel harder than they should.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless more often than you used to?
I don’t think so… not really fidgety. Mostly I’m just tired.
Do you find yourself pacing back and forth or feeling like you need to be in constant motion?
No… I don’t think so. I’m not pacing around or anything. If anything, I’m more just… slow, I guess.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations or delusions besides hearing the man's voice when you're mopping?

I mean… yeah, maybe. I get this thought that the landlord, and a couple people in the building, are kind of watching me through the hallway cameras. Like they’re keeping tabs, maybe passing things around about me. People say the cameras are just for the front door, but… I don’t know. It’s hard to shake.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or like you need to move around when you're sitting or lying down?
Not really. When I’m sitting or lying down, I mostly just feel worn out… I don’t feel like I have to get up and move.
Do you find yourself doing more physical activity than usual, like walking around or engaging in other movements, when you're feeling down or upset?
No… I haven’t really noticed that. When I’m down, I’m usually more still than active. I might do what I have to do, but not extra walking around or anything.
Are you feeling down or depressed for most of the day, every day?

Yeah… most days, I guess. Since I moved, it’s kind of been there in the background a lot—feeling sad, tired, not really interested in much. Even when I’m more caught up thinking about other things, it’s still there.
Have you had any periods where your depression seemed to lift or get significantly better, even if only for a short time, since you started feeling this way?

Yeah… there was a little while, maybe a few weeks, where it wasn’t as heavy. I was eating a bit more normal and getting through work a little better.

But… some things didn’t really stop. I’d still hear my name in the stairwell, and I still felt like the hallway cameras were being used to keep track of me.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt completely back to normal since your depression started?
No… I don’t think I’ve felt completely normal for two weeks straight. The low part’s been going on maybe… a year and a couple months, since not long after I moved.
